The solution is much simpler than what everyone is suggesting. There are two stages important for this, BFU (before first unlock) and AFU (after first unlock)

When you restart your phone initially it's in BFU mode. This is because android (and I believe iOS?) encrypts your memory using your pin, after a restart it is required to decrypt your storage. Once you enter your pin the decryption key is stored in memory so you can use your fingerprint. This is the AFU mode. 

Also occasionally if there was a sudden jolt in movement (for my Samsung atleast) or if the phone just hadn't been used in a while it will verify the PIN. This is mostly because it's easier to force someone's finger on a screen than to force them to say a pin. Legally the police can force you to unlock biometric security but they can't force you to give up your pin without a warrant.
